name: FRANK MANGA+ v1.3.2

# FRANK MANGA+ v1.3.2

This patch release restores image rendering in the Windows build.

## Windows image rendering (#21)

Windows WebView2 represents Tauri custom protocols as an HTTP-shaped local
URL. The reader previously emitted the native `mpimg://` form directly, so
cover and chapter image requests never reached the Rust image proxy on
Windows.

Image sources now use Tauri's platform-aware URL conversion. The Rust handler
decodes both the Windows and native forms, preserves signed MANGA Plus CDN
queries, and accepts only HTTPS targets on the MANGA Plus CDN boundary.

## Dependency and security maintenance

- Patched WebPKI certificate and root-store crates resolve the three current
  RustSec vulnerabilities without changing the CDN-fingerprint-sensitive
  `wreq` and `wreq-util` pins.
- Compatible Tauri CLI, Vite, Vitest, and Svelte-check patch updates are
  included. A patched `cookie` override clears the advisory inherited through
  the current SvelteKit 2 release line without adopting breaking framework
  major versions.
- `cargo audit` and `bun audit` report no known vulnerabilities. The remaining
  RustSec notices are upstream maintenance/unsoundness warnings in Tauri's
  Linux GTK dependency graph.

## Tests and verification

- New regression tests cover the Windows and native custom-protocol URL forms,
  signed-query preservation, retry cache busting, non-Tauri rendering, and
  rejection of untrusted proxy targets.
- All 179 Vitest tests and 70 desktop Rust tests pass.
- A live device-registration/profile smoke test passed after the trust-store
  updates; the exact CDN TLS-fingerprint pins remain unchanged.
- `./verify.sh` is green: Rust tests and Clippy, Vitest, `svelte-check`, the
  production frontend build, and Vite development CSS probes.

# FRANK MANGA+ v1.3.1

This patch release keeps your reading position stable when the app window
changes size and refreshes compatible dependencies.

## Keep reading position across window resizes (#17)

Resizing the window, docking or undocking a laptop, or otherwise changing the
display geometry no longer moves the reader to a different page. The reader
anchors the first visible page for the entire resize burst and restores it
after layout settles, without saving transient pages as reading progress.

Pending restoration is cancelled when the reader changes chapters or unmounts,
so a resize from the previous chapter cannot affect newly loaded pages.

## Dependency and security maintenance

- Compatible Tauri, Svelte, Vite, and TypeScript definition updates are
  included without adopting breaking framework major versions.
- CI and release workflows use the Node 24-based `actions/checkout` and
  `actions/cache` releases, pinned to verified immutable commits.
- The Rust dependency graph updates `quinn-proto` and `rustls`, resolving the
  published advisories present in v1.3.0.
- The exact `wreq` and `wreq-util` versions required for the MANGA Plus CDN TLS
  fingerprint remain pinned and were verified with a live authenticated API
  registration/profile smoke test.

## Tests and verification

- New regression tests cover resize bursts, inactive readers, and cancellation
  during reader-state reset. 178 Vitest tests total.
- A browser-level smoke test verified that page 4 remains page 4 after a resize
  and after a rapid resize burst.
- `./verify.sh` is green: Rust tests and Clippy, Vitest, `svelte-check`, the

# FRANK MANGA+ v1.3.0

Manual pairing corrections for chapters whose spreads are not marked by the
MANGA Plus API.

## Fix unmarked double-page spreads per chapter (#13, closes #12)

Double-page mode still follows authoritative RIGHT/LEFT spread markers
automatically. When a chapter has no markers, you can now press `P` or click
the pairing-shift icon at a wrongly paired frame to shift pairing from that
point. Page 1 toggles the cover rule; a later selected page becomes solo and
the following pages resume with the opposite pairing.

- A correction on page 1 switches between a solo cover and pairing from the
  first page.
- Later corrections handle chapters whose spread parity changes partway
  through, including chapters that need more than one adjustment.
- Corrections persist per chapter across sessions.
- Removing a correction also clears later corrections whose parity depended
  on it.
- Chapters with API-marked spreads keep automatic grouping and ignore stale
  manual corrections.

The help dialog documents the new shortcut, and the spread-pairing audit now
records fresh live-API evidence for English and Brazilian Portuguese editions
(#11).

## Security hardening

- Device secrets are written atomically and restricted to the current user on
  Unix (`0700` config directory, `0600` secret file). Existing permissive files
  are hardened when read, symlink targets are rejected, and credentials never
  fall back to a shared temporary directory.
- `rustls` is updated to 0.23.45, resolving RUSTSEC-2026-0285.
- Every GitHub Action is pinned to an immutable, verified commit. Release jobs
  use least-privilege token permissions and validate release tags before using
  them in shell commands.

## Tests + verification

- Reader grouping and persistence tests cover initial and later shifts,
  multiple corrections, removal dependencies, chapter boundaries, malformed
  stored data, and protection for API-marked chapters. 175 Vitest tests total.
- Backend tests cover private secret-file permissions, migration, atomic
  replacement, missing persistent config, and symlink rejection.
- `./verify.sh` on merged `main`: all green — Rust tests/clippy, Vitest,

name: FRANK MANGA+ v1.2.0
body:
# FRANK MANGA+ v1.2.0

Spread-aware double-page layout.

## Two layouts instead of three, paired as printed (#10, closes #9)

The reader's double-page mode now reads the API's spread markers instead of
pairing pages blindly by position.

Previously there were three layouts — `single`, `double` (pairs from page 1),
and `double-cover` (cover solo, then pairs) — and a two-page spread only
stayed whole when its halves happened to land on the parity of the layout you
picked. You had to cycle layouts with `D` per title until spreads lined up,
and no single layout worked for every title.

`manga_viewer_v3` is requested with `split=yes`, which delivers each spread as
a RIGHT half followed by its LEFT half (`MangaPage.type`). The reader now uses
those markers:

- **single** — unchanged.
- **double** — facing pages, paired the way each chapter was printed. The
  chapter's first spread fixes where its pairs start: cover binds solo, or
  pairs start on page 1 when the cover itself is a spread. A split spread
  always shares one frame; if a later spread would fall off the chapter's
  parity, the page before it renders solo rather than cutting the spread. The
  decision resets at every chapter boundary.

`D` now toggles `single ↔ double`. A saved `double-cover` preference (global
or per-title) is read as `double`, so no setting is lost.

Known limitation (documented in `reader/docs/spread-pairing-audit.md`): a few
titles — One Piece ch1–3 among them — deliver real spreads *unmarked* as
consecutive single pages. Detection can't fire there, so those chapters use
the cover-solo default, which matches print for them by parity. An
image-based fallback is noted for future work.

## Tests + verification

- 11 new `buildPageGroups` unit cases built from live chapter layouts (Hey!
  Devil Girl! #001, Home at the Horizon #001): cover-solo, cover-as-spread,
  even/odd first-spread offsets, off-parity spreads, orphan halves, and
  chapter-boundary safety. 166 vitest tests total.
- `./verify.sh` on merged main: all green — Rust tests/clippy, Vitest,
  `svelte-check`, production build, and Vite dev CSS probe. CI green on the
  merge commit across ubuntu/macos/windows.

# FRANK MANGA+ v1.1.2

Chapter-list clarity and a redesigned content-language picker.

## Chapter list no longer looks broken when you're caught up

Reading the newest chapters made the title page look wrong: with "Unread
only" on (the default), every chapter you'd read was hidden, so the list
appeared to *end* at your newest unread chapter (e.g. #122) while "Continue"
jumped to a later, already-read chapter (#131). Nothing was actually wrong —
but there was no way to tell.

- A clear cue now sits above the list whenever read chapters are hidden:
  **"N read chapters hidden · show all"**, one click to reveal them. The
  newest chapters never silently vanish again.
- The count header was reworded. "122 unread of 134" read like a chapter
  position ("chapter 122 of 134"); it's now **"134 total · 12 read · 122
  unread"**, which can't be misread.

Note on totals: 134 is correct — a title's chapter list legitimately
includes bonus ("ex") chapters alongside the numbered ones, and those are
real, readable, and counted.

## Redesigned content-language picker

The row of nine pill buttons in the header (EN ESP FRA IND PT-BR RUS THA VIE
DEU) was replaced with a single compact dropdown: a globe + current-selection
summary ("EN", "EN, ESP", "EN +3", or "All languages") that opens a clean
checklist. It stays a multi-select — pick as many catalogs to merge as you
like — and the last active language can't be switched off, same as before.

- New unit coverage for the language-summary label and the reworded
  chapter-count label (159 vitest tests total).

body: # FRANK MANGA+ v1.1.1 Patch release: the reader's broken-image recovery actually recovers now, and a suspended laptop can no longer wedge image loading for good. ## Reader image recovery - The broken-image retry — both the automatic retry ladder and the manual "↻ Reload page" button — used to change only the URL **fragment** (`#attempt=N`). Per the HTML spec, an `` whose src changes only in the fragment is never re-fetched, so every retry was a no-op; leaving the chapter and re-entering was the only recovery. After the machine sleeps (laptop lid closed), a dead pooled connection would hang a fetch until the OS TCP timeout (~15 min) — and a hung fetch holds an image-fetch slot the whole time, so enough of them parked every slot and nothing would ever load again until restart. body:
# FRANK MANGA+ v1.1.0

Feature release: content-language selection across the nine MANGA Plus catalogs, and a chapter list that surfaces what you haven't read yet.

## Content languages

- A picker in the header selects any combination of the nine catalogs — EN, ESP, FRA, IND, PT-BR, RUS, THA, VIE, DEU. The selection drives Search, Library, title detail, and the reader, persists across sessions (`mp:contentLanguages`), and never empties: the last active language can't be switched off.
- Search fetches the selected catalogs and merges them in fixed header order, so editions of the same work (MANGA Plus issues a separate titleId per translation) sit side by side. Library filters the same way: other editions of a favorite are hidden, not removed, and reappear when their language is re-selected. Non-English covers carry a language badge.
- The `Title.language` wire-enum map was inferred and three values were wrong (ind/ptb/rus sat on each other's numbers). Corrected and now pinned two ways: recorded protobuf fixtures for all nine catalogs, and agreement with the official app's own proto. Enum 8 is ITALIAN there; no Italian catalog exists, so it stays unmapped.
- Outbound `lang`/`clang` are clamped to the supported set (case-insensitive, English default) instead of reaching the API verbatim, and `title_detail`/`manga_viewer` responses are validated against the requested edition — a mismatch is an error, not a silent substitution, so chapter navigation can't wander into another translation.
- The Rust catalog/cache paths now filter by `clang` (catalog language) instead of `lang` (interface language). Caches written by older builds with the wrong filter are evicted and refetched instead of serving an empty catalog for the rest of the TTL.

## Hide read chapters

- A title's chapter list now hides read chapters by default — opening a long-running series shows what's left to read instead of everything ever published. A toggle next to the sort button cycles **unread only → read collapsed → all chapters** and persists (`mp:readVis`). When everything is read, a "Show all chapters" escape hatch appears so the list can never strand you.
- Rows are no longer uniform height (a collapsed read row is a slim line), so the virtualizer binary-searches a prefix-sum height table instead of dividing by a constant.

## Docs and repo

- New `docs/ios-secret.md`: extracting a subscriber `deviceSecret` on iOS via mitmproxy, linked from the README, install guide, and troubleshooting page. Thanks @Zindre17.
- `README.es-ES.md`: full Spanish translation of the README. Thanks @webbrain-one.
- Release-build gotcha documented: bare `cargo build --release` silently embeds the dev URL — use `bun run tauri build --no-bundle`.
- `mise.toml` moved off the deprecated `python = "system"` pin to `[settings] disable_tools`.

body:
# FRANK MANGA+ v1.0.2

Stability release: expired-URL recovery and image-cache garbage collection.

## Signed-URL expiry recovery (broken pages after sleep / long sessions)

- Page image URLs are signed with an `expires=` timestamp valid for roughly
  1-2 hours, and premium fetches also depend on the `plus_vw_token` cookie
  minted by the same `manga_viewer_v3` call. After a long idle or a
  sleep/wake cycle both go stale: re-requested pages hit the CDN with a dead
  signature, and the Reload button re-requested that same dead URL forever —
  the "broken placeholder at best" loop.
- The reader now detects expired signatures (with a 5-minute safety margin)
  and re-fetches the owning chapter to mint fresh URLs — refreshing the
  cookie as a side effect — then swaps them into the page list in place.
  Retry bookkeeping for replaced URLs is dropped so it can't accumulate.
- Recovery triggers from four directions: image error on an expired URL,
  the manual Reload button / R key, window visibilitychange (wake/refocus),
  and a minutely background sweep — which also covers machines that sleep
  with the window visible and slow reads that outlive the signature.

## Image-cache garbage collection

- The on-disk image cache was never evicted and grew unboundedly (observed:
  4.8 GB across 10,011 files). A startup GC now prunes the image subtree to
  a byte budget — oldest-mtime files first, so recently read chapters stay
  warm. Default budget 2048 MB; `MANGAPLUS_IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_MB` overrides.
  The catalog SWR cache is never touched.

## Tests + verification

- 5 new Rust tests for the cache GC (oldest-first order, budget edges,
  empty-directory cleanup, missing dir, zero budget) and 5 new vitest cases
  for expiry parsing and margin behavior — 100 vitest + 29 Rust tests total.

# FRANK MANGA+ v1.0.1

Reading-flow fix: aggressive image preloading.

## Sliding eager-load window

- Previously only the first 3 pages of a chapter were eager-loaded;
  everything else relied on browser-native lazy loading, which starts a
  fetch only when the image is nearly on screen. With full-viewport page
  frames and flip/jump navigation, the reader routinely landed on an empty
  placeholder and made the user wait (or wiggle back and forth) for the
  page to appear.
- Images now use a sliding eager window around the reading position:
  10 pages ahead and 3 behind are always fetching, following the reader as
  they advance. Far-away pages stay lazy so opening a chapter doesn't pull
  an entire title's worth of `super_high` images at once.
- The window pairs with the existing next-chapter prefetch (which fires
  8 pages from the end of the loaded scroll), so freshly appended chapter
  pages start downloading as soon as they enter the window.

## Tests + verification

- New unit coverage for the window logic: edges ahead/behind, lazy outside
  the window, and full eager coverage of a freshly opened chapter's first
  pages (95 vitest tests total).
- `./verify.sh`: all green — Rust tests/clippy, Vitest, `svelte-check`,
  production build, and Vite dev CSS probe.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v1.0.0
body:
# FRANK MANGA+ v1.0.0

The 1.0 release. What started as a decompiled-XAPK experiment in May is now a
complete daily-driver desktop reader for MANGA Plus: full catalog browsing and
search, a distraction-free chapter reader with seamless auto-advance, per-title
layout preferences, resilient image loading — and, as of this release, full
awareness of the MANGA Plus MAX subscription model, from lock badges in the
chapter list to a proactive warning when your plan lapses server-side.

## Subscription awareness (new in this release)

### Real API error messages

- The API's `ErrorResult.english_popup` (subject + body) is now decoded and
  surfaced. A refused chapter says `API error: Invalid user: Invalid user
  access(11301) (action=0)` instead of the old
  `code=Some("action=0") action=None english=None`.
- Fallback order: English popup → `debug_info` → bare action code.

### Visible paywall

- Chapter lists now badge subscription-locked chapters: 🔒 **MAX**
  (standard tier), 🔒 **MAX Deluxe**, or 🔒 **Locked** (locked after free
  read), driven by the API's `chapter_type` field.
- Opening a locked chapter your plan doesn't cover shows a friendly
  "subscription-locked" explanation with a Back-to-title button instead of a
  raw error and a useless Retry.
- Auto-advance that prefetches into a locked chapter now says so, instead of
  the misleading "may be rate-limited" retry loop.

### Plan-drop warning (why chapters suddenly stop loading)

- Root cause documented: the server-side entitlement is backed by a Google
  Play receipt only the official app can refresh; when the attested billing
  period ends the account silently downgrades to `basic` and MAX-tier
  chapters refuse with error 11301.
- The Library page now polls `GET /api/subscription` (at most every 12h) and
  shows a dismissible amber banner when the plan drops below the best plan
  seen, or when the billing period ends without renewing server-side.
- New `get_subscription` Tauri command + `SubscriptionView`/`UserSubscription`
  proto messages (SuccessResult field 36).
- The restore ritual (rooted AVD + official app), including the emulator DNS
  flag and the stale-mitmproxy-setting gotcha, is documented in
  `reader/docs/android-secret.md`.

## Dependency updates

- Frontend (within semver): svelte 5.57.0, @tauri-apps/plugin-opener 2.5.5,
  transitive refreshes. Majors deferred to post-1.0 (Vite 8, TypeScript 7,
  vite-plugin-svelte 7, vitest 5).
- Rust: routine `cargo update`; `wreq`/`wreq-util` stay exact-pinned at
  rc.28/rc.11 (TLS fingerprint).

## Tests + verification

- New coverage: server-error popup mapping (2 unit tests), live-captured
  fixtures for the 11301 refusal and the subscription view, lock-label and
  lock-error helpers, and 11 subscription-warning decision tests. 92 vitest
  tests total.
- `./verify.sh`: all green — Rust tests/clippy, Vitest, `svelte-check`,
  production build, and Vite dev CSS probe.

# FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.7

Reader immersion release: the page now owns the whole window, with auto-hiding bars.

## Auto-hiding reader bars

- The reader header and footer collapse 2 seconds after opening a chapter, and again 2 seconds after the mouse leaves them.
- Both bars are now fixed overlays that slide in/out over the page, so pages render at the full window height instead of subtracting the bar heights.
- Moving the mouse to the very top edge of the window slides the header back in; the very bottom edge brings back the footer/progress bar.
- Edge detection uses a window `mousemove` listener rather than invisible hover strips, so page-turn clicks near the edges are never swallowed.
- While the pointer is over a bar it stays open indefinitely; the hide countdown only arms once the pointer leaves.

## Dependency updates

- Frontend (within semver): Svelte 5.56.10, SvelteKit 2.70.3, svelte-check 4.7.6, Vite 6.4.3, Vitest 4.1.11, @tauri-apps/api 2.11.1, @tauri-apps/cli 2.11.4, @types/node 25.9.5.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.5
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.5

Svelte event-system hardening release: fewer UI lockups, better retry paths, stronger race guards, and a clean local verification run.

### UI responsiveness + error handling

- Added a shared IPC timeout helper so hung Tauri calls surface as retryable UI errors instead of infinite spinners.
- Search now registers the `all_titles_refreshed` listener before catalog fetches can trigger background refreshes, and cleans up safely if navigation happens while `listen()` is still resolving.
- Title detail renders as soon as the main detail request completes; favorite state loads independently so a slow library call no longer blocks the whole page.
- Title favorite add/remove failures now show a user-visible error instead of failing silently.
- Secret setup IPC calls now use the same timeout handling and avoid treating a secondary `is_auto_registered` failure as a failed configuration check.

### Race-condition guards

- Title and reader routes now reload on same-route param changes (`/title/1 -> /title/2`, `/reader/1 -> /reader/2`) and ignore stale async completions from older params.
- Reader chapter fetches reuse an in-flight promise per chapter/locale, so a frontend timeout plus manual retry does not duplicate backend work.
- Search favorite retry timers no longer clear a newer pending retry state.
- Reader image retry timers are cleared on success, manual retry, bulk reload, route reset, and unmount.
- Page-flip animation now captures the DOM node before async waits so unmounts cannot corrupt cleanup.

### Cleanups + tests

- Fixed all `svelte-check` errors and Help modal accessibility warnings.
- Added `@types/node` so Vite config no longer needs a stale `@ts-expect-error`.
- Added focused Vitest coverage for IPC timeout formatting/behavior and favorite error-state cleanup.
- Updated `verify.sh` to warm Svelte modules before checking virtual dev CSS chunks and reject raw Svelte payloads, matching how Vite/Svelte actually serves those endpoints.
- Added `AGENTS.md` with compact repo-specific guidance for future OpenCode sessions.

### Verification

- `./verify.sh`: all green — Rust tests/clippy, Vitest, `svelte-check`, production build, and Vite dev CSS probe.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.4
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.4

Full-catalog search via a stale-while-revalidate cache; fast thumbnail loading; library-state-aware "+ Library" button. Big internal cleanup pass — every new code path was audited and hardened before shipping.

### Search

- The search page now uses the full MANGA Plus catalog (~thousands of titles, fetched from `title_list/all_v3`) rather than only the curated ~531 in `title_list/search`. Titles like "Bleach" that exist in the catalog but not in the curated list now turn up when you type.
- The curated catalog still loads on mount for the fast landing view; the full catalog is lazy-fetched the first time you type a character. Subsequent keystrokes filter against it instantly.
- Results capped at 80 visible with a "Showing first N of M — refine your query" footer.
- "+ Library" button now reflects state: `+ Library`, `Adding…`, `✓ In Library`, or `Retry`. Buttons disable while in-flight or already added.

### Cache (`~/.cache/mangaplus-reader/all_titles_<lang>_<clang>.bin`)

- Stale-while-revalidate. First read: blocks on network. Within 24h: serves from disk instantly. After 24h: still serves from disk *and* kicks off a background refresh that emits an `all_titles_refreshed` Tauri event when fresh data lands.
- TTL configurable via `MANGAPLUS_CATALOG_TTL_HOURS=N`.
- Atomic writes via `*.tmp` + rename — a crash mid-write never leaves the bin/meta pair inconsistent.
- Per-locale dogpile guard so 10 simultaneous stale reads spawn one refresh, not ten.
- Decode failures (old shape, truncated, corrupt) evict the bad files and fall through to a fresh fetch — no `rm -rf` required by the user.
- Filter applied on both write *and* read paths so caches written by older builds correct themselves transparently.

### Image fetching (thumbnails + chapter pages)

- The previous behaviour serialized **every** image fetch behind the 500ms API rate-limit mutex — a cold-cache 80-thumbnail grid took 40 seconds to populate. The API mutex is now scoped to actual API calls; CDN fetches use a separate 12-permit semaphore for genuine parallelism.
- Cache-hit fast path skips the semaphore entirely — re-renders never queue behind in-flight network fetches.
- Per-image retry with exponential backoff: 250ms → 500ms → 1s on transient failures (timeout, connection reset, 408, 429, 5xx). Hard 4xx (404, 403…) fail fast.
- **Critical fix from the audit:** backoff sleeps now happen *without* holding the semaphore permit. The earlier version pinned a permit for the full ~1.75s backoff window, collapsing effective concurrency under retries.
- Image body size cap: 32 MB. Defends against a misbehaving CDN streaming gigabytes.

### Robustness — what the pre-release audit caught

A three-agent code review surfaced 14 issues. The 8 most impactful were fixed before shipping; the other 6 were addressed as a "make it robust" pass after the user asked for nothing-deferred.

- **Partial-success on `tokio::join!`**: a 429 on either of the two catalog buckets no longer loses the whole refresh. Whatever succeeded is persisted; both-failed surfaces the error.
- **Permit released before backoff sleep** (see above).
- **Cache decode fall-through**: a corrupt cache evicts itself and triggers a network refetch instead of stuck-with-no-recovery.
- **Locale matching captured in component state**, not module constants — a future language switcher won't drop in-flight refresh events.
- **Unknown-language canary**: a one-time stderr warn fires the first time MANGA Plus ships a new language enum value we haven't mapped, so the new titles don't silently disappear from filtered results.
- **Case-insensitive locale matching**: `"ESP"` no longer silently falls through to English titles.
- **Refresh-skipped log** when the dogpile guard blocks a duplicate refresh — visibility into a previously silent path.

### Code structure

- Pure logic extracted to:
  - `reader/desktop/src-tauri/src/all_titles_cache.rs` — SWR disk-cache mechanics (16 tests).
  - `reader/desktop/src/lib/searchLogic.ts` — `flattenSearchView`, `filterTitles`, `paginate`, `computeButtonLabel`, `buttonDisabled` (21 vitest cases).
  - `merge_views` + `filter_to_language` + `backoff_delay_ms` in Rust (12 new unit tests).
- `get_all_titles_cached` split into a three-step pipeline: `serve_from_cache` → `fetch_and_merge` → `persist_titles`.
- Magic numbers (`12`, `2`, `250ms`, `32 MB`, shift cap `8`) all promoted to named constants with explanations.

### Tests + lints

- **73 cargo tests** (was 47): 13 api + 60 desktop.
- **70 vitest** (was 49): 21 new in `searchLogic.test.ts`.
- **Clippy clean** on `--workspace --lib --tests`.
- **svelte-check**: only pre-existing errors remain; nothing new from this diff.

### Per-commit log

```
single bundled commit (audit + fixes were interleaved)
```

### Backwards compatibility

- Cache files written by any prior build (which decoded into a different shape) are now evicted gracefully on first read; you don't need to delete anything by hand.
- The `lang_str_to_enum` table mirrors `src/lib/lang.ts` exactly — adding a new language requires a one-line addition on both sides (caught by a canary log line in production).
- No changes to the v0.9.0 render-mode policy or the v0.9.3 page-sizing.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.3
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.3

Reader page-sizing follow-up to v0.9.2.

### What was broken

v0.9.2 made `.page-frame` viewport-fit-height (`min-height: calc(100vh - 88px)`), but `.manga-page` kept `max-height: …` — a cap, not a force. Series with shorter intrinsic page dimensions (Akane-banashi pages are ~836×900 vs the more common ~836×1200) rendered at their natural height inside an oversized frame, leaving black letterbox above and below.

### Fix

One CSS change: replace `max-height` with `height` on `.manga-page` so images scale **up** to fill the frame, not just down to cap. Width stays `auto` so aspect ratio is preserved.

```css
.manga-page {
  height: calc(100vh - 48px - 32px - 8px);  /* was: max-height */
  width: auto;
  max-width: 100%;
  …
}
```

Single-page and double-pair modes both improve; `vh` keeps it dynamic on window resize. 49 vitest pass.

### Edge cases

- **Pair mode**: the wrapper still has `max-width: 50%`, so typical aspect ratios fit comfortably. Very wide spreads (e.g. 1672×1200 at viewport 992 height) would want more than 50% width and may slightly distort — those are uncommon in practice.
- **Very narrow windows** (<500px): `max-width: 100%` may cause slight horizontal distortion. Not catastrophic.

### Backwards compatibility

Pure CSS change. No effect on render-mode policy, prefetch logic, or end-of-title gating from v0.9.0–v0.9.2.

name: v0.9.2 — reader chapter-boundary robustness pass
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.2

Reader robustness pass. A handful of small bugs around chapter boundaries that compounded into a confusing experience.

### What was broken

Five issues, all on the chapter-transition path:

1. **End-of-title flag flashed at the start of new chapters.** The viewer-side `chapters` list is truncated to a small window around the current chapter. When a new chapter loaded, that window briefly said "no next chapter exists" until the canonical list from `title_detail` resolved. The 🏁 "You've reached the end" block surfaced for a half-second every time, then disappeared. Confusing for first-time users.
2. **Space / PageDown didn't always advance to page 1 of the next chapter.** After a cross-chapter scroll, `currentGroup` wasn't updated until the `IntersectionObserver` settled the new frame past 50% visibility. The next keystroke fired `advance()` with the *old* `currentGroup` value, so the keyboard appeared to do nothing — only mouse-scroll worked because that updated the observer manually.
3. **Sometimes the next chapter wasn't prefetched in time.** Trigger distance was 5 pages from end. On slow connections you'd finish reading before the API responded, see "loading next chapter…" and a brief blank screen.
4. **Pages didn't stretch to viewport height on some titles.** Akane-banashi pages in particular — short images and a `.page-frame` that sized to the image rather than the viewport meant scroll-snap couldn't settle cleanly. Tops of the next pages peeked at the bottom of the screen.
5. **Image placeholders collapsed when the proto returned zero dimensions.** Rare, but when it happened the wrapper was 0×0 until bytes arrived, so the layout shifted noticeably as each image loaded.

### Fixes

- **`titleDetailLoaded` flag** gates the end-of-title block. While the canonical list is still in flight, a soft "checking for more chapters…" indicator shows instead. End-of-title only renders once we know the catalog has nothing more.
- **`goToGroupIndex` now sets `currentGroup` immediately**, before the smooth scroll completes. The observer still reconfirms it on settle, but the keyboard no longer races the scroll animation.
- **`PREFETCH_TRIGGER_DISTANCE` bumped from 5 to 8.** Three extra pages of reading buffer for slow API responses. No downside — prefetched chapters that go unread cost a few hundred KB of cache.
- **`.page-frame` is now `min-height: calc(100vh - 88px)` with flex centering.** Each frame reserves the full viewport, scroll-snap settles cleanly, dynamic on resize because it's in `vh`. The `.manga-page` keeps its intrinsic aspect ratio via `max-height` of the same value.
- **Image `width`/`height` attrs fall back to 836×1200** (typical MANGA Plus page) when the proto returned zeroes. Wrapper reserves the right space before bytes arrive.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.0
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.9.0

Linux render policy + auto-recovery. **Most users get GPU acceleration back.**

### What changed

Through v0.8.0 the binary unconditionally set `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` on Linux — full CPU rendering for everyone, just to keep the ~5% of users on broken EGL setups working. v0.9.0 replaces that hammer with a tiered policy that picks the lightest workaround for your actual hardware, and auto-recovers if it gets the wrong answer.

### The new policy

On every Linux launch, the binary now reads:

1. `MANGAPLUS_RENDER_MODE` env var (user override)
2. `~/.config/mangaplus-reader/render.conf` (`mode = ...`, persistent override)
3. `~/.config/mangaplus-reader/render-recovery` marker (previous launch died?)
4. GPU vendor from `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/vendor`
5. Display server from `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `$DISPLAY`

…then picks one of four modes:

| Mode | Env vars set | When auto-detect picks it |
|---|---|---|
| `native` | none — full GPU, WebKit defaults | X11 sessions |
| `dmabuf-off` | `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` | Wayland + AMD or Intel (SHM compositing still GPU-accelerated) |
| `nvidia-light` | + `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` | Wayland + NVIDIA |
| `safe` | + `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` | Crash recovery (last launch failed) |

Whatever it applied lives in `~/.config/mangaplus-reader/render-state.log` — `cat` that file to see exactly what your binary is doing.

### Auto-recovery

Startup touches the recovery marker; the frontend deletes it on first successful render via a new `mark_app_ready` Tauri command. If the WebView aborts before that fires (the classic blank-white-screen EGL crash), the marker stays behind. The **next** launch reads the marker → falls back to `safe` mode automatically → working app, no docs needed.

This means a Bazzite + AMD + KWin Wayland user (issue [#1](https://github.com/akitaonrails/frank_mangaplus/issues/1)) hitting `EGL_BAD_PARAMETER` on first launch now gets a working app on the second launch with no intervention.

### Manual overrides

Quick test (single launch):

```bash
MANGAPLUS_RENDER_MODE=safe ./FRANK.MANGA+_*_amd64.AppImage
# also: native, dmabuf-off, nvidia-light, auto
```

Persistent — `~/.config/mangaplus-reader/render.conf`:

```
mode = nvidia-light
```

The env var wins if both are set.

### New `docs/troubleshooting.md`

Walks through every mode, the auto-recovery loop, common scenarios (blank screen, sluggish flip, "worked yesterday"), and the last-resort escape hatches (`GDK_BACKEND=x11`, `WEBKIT_FORCE_SANDBOX=0`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`). Linked from the README header nav and the install section.

### Tests + code structure

Everything decision-making lives in `src-tauri/src/render_env.rs` as pure functions; `lib.rs::run()` is just side-effecting wiring. The integration is small enough to inspect at a glance.

**25 new Rust tests** covering:
- `parse_vendor_hex` across casing/prefix variants
- `RenderMode::env_vars` layering
- `decide_mode` for every `(display, gpu)` combo + explicit override + recovery precedence
- `resolve_user_override` (env wins over config, garbage fall-through, neither set)
- Recovery marker lifecycle (create / clear / idempotent)
- `parse_config_mode` with comments, quotes, multi-key files
- `write_state_log` content shape for both Native (no env) and NvidiaLight (env listed)

**29 desktop crate tests total** (was 4 before this batch). Frontend vitest unchanged at 49. Clippy clean on `--lib --tests` for both crates.

### Per-commit log

```

701e2d1 feat(layout): mark_app_ready handshake clears the crash-recovery marker
326a70d feat(desktop): wire render_env policy into lib.rs::run + mark_app_ready
d4b71d4 feat(desktop): crash-recovery marker + user-override config
ddc765b feat(desktop): render_env module — GPU detection + render-mode policy
```

### Backwards compatibility

If you had a working v0.8.0 install, **nothing changes for you** unless you're on Linux. Linux users on:

- **X11**: get GPU acceleration back (was force-disabled in v0.8.0)
- **Wayland + AMD / Intel**: get GPU compositing back via SHM
- **Wayland + NVIDIA**: get GPU compositing back via the explicit-sync workaround
- **Bazzite-style broken EGL combos**: still work, via auto-recovery → safe mode on the second launch

If anything regresses for you on Linux, set `MANGAPLUS_RENDER_MODE=safe` to get the v0.8.0 behaviour back, and please file an issue with your `render-state.log` contents.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.8.0
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.8.0

Reader features + reliability batch — six commits, all individually tested.

### New features

**Home / End jump keys.** Press <kbd>Home</kbd> to jump to the first page of the chapter you're reading, <kbd>End</kbd> for the last. Works in every layout mode.

**In-app help modal.** Press <kbd>?</kbd> or click the new question-mark button in the header to open a list of every keybinding and the click-zone layout. Auto-opens once on the user's very first chapter (latched via `localStorage` so it doesn't keep appearing).

**Broken-image recovery.** If a page fails to load — the CDN sometimes drops a request mid-fetch — the reader now does up to 3 silent auto-retries with a short delay between attempts. Most transient blips clear without you noticing. Only after the auto-budget is exhausted does the empty slot show a `↻ Reload page N` button overlay; press <kbd>R</kbd> to retry every failed image in the chapter at once.

### Reliability + perf

**Chapter-boundary advance lands on page 1 of the new chapter, every time.** Two root causes fixed:

- `advance()` used to scroll to `currentGroup + 1` *after* awaiting the prefetch. `currentGroup` can drift during the wait if the `IntersectionObserver` re-fires, so the post-await scroll targeted whatever-stale-position + 1. Now `advance()` looks up the new chapter's first group by ID via a new pure helper (`firstGroupOfChapter`), which is immune to that drift.
- Rapid tapping at a boundary queued multiple in-flight `advance()` calls, each with its own stale lookup. New re-entrancy guard drops duplicate calls while one is in progress.

**Night-mode filter no longer makes page-flip animation sluggish.** Filter is now applied to each `.manga-page` individually instead of to the whole `.page-stack`. Each image's filtered output is cached on the img itself; transforms on the stack move already-filtered surfaces around without re-rasterising the entire scroll content per frame.

**Earlier background prefetch.** `PREFETCH_TRIGGER_DISTANCE` bumped from 2 → 5. Gives the network roundtrip more time to finish before the user hits the chapter boundary.

### Tests + refactor

Pure logic for every keybinding, chapter-boundary lookup, and group-finding helper lives in `lib/readerLogic.ts` with `lib/readerLogic.test.ts` coverage. Six new vitest cases landed this release:

- Home / End → chapter-jump actions
- `?` → open-help
- `R` / `r` → reload-images
- `firstGroupOfChapter` for single mode, double mode, missing-chapter, and the regression case (108-page chapter then 43-page chapter, land on page 109)

49 vitest cases passing.

### Per-commit log

body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.6

Second-stage Wayland fix — addresses [#1](https://github.com/akitaonrails/frank_mangaplus/issues/1).

### What was broken

v0.5.2 added `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` to bypass the `Could not create GBM EGL display: EGL_SUCCESS. Aborting…` crash on Wayland. That covered the GBM/DMABUF code path inside WebKitGTK.

A user reported a *different* EGL failure on Bazzite (Fedora atomic) + AMD Lucienne integrated GPU + KWin Wayland:

```
Could not create default EGL display: EGL_BAD_PARAMETER. Aborting...
```

That's the SHM (software-mapped) compositing path failing as well. The window mounts (title bar appears), the WebView aborts before painting anything, you see a blank white panel.

### What changed

The binary now also sets `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` at startup, pushing WebKit into full CPU-side compositing — no EGL at all. Combined with the existing DMABUF disable, this covers both reported EGL initialisation failures.

Performance impact for our use case is negligible: manga pages are mostly static; the page-flip animation and CSS sepia filter run on the CPU without any visible drop. Browsers do *much* heavier compositing — a static image viewer is roughly free.

Both env vars are still set conditionally — if you've already set either yourself (`export WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=0` to force hardware compositing back on, say), the binary respects your value.

### If you still see EGL crashes

A few escalations worth trying as env vars before launch:

- `WEBKIT_FORCE_SANDBOX=0` — disables WebKit's process sandbox (some distros block EGL there)
- `GDK_BACKEND=x11` — forces XWayland; EGL sometimes works on the X path when native Wayland doesn't
- `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — last resort, full software rendering of the entire GL stack

If none of those work, file an issue with `inxi -G` (or `fastfetch`) output and the AppImage launch logs.

body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.5

Reader-page audit + refactor. No new user-facing features — the goal is making the reader's behaviour consistent and the regressions impossible.

### What was audited

State (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`), every event handler, every key binding, every async path, every set/get on reactive variables, every `scrollIntoView` call site. Findings:

1. `loadedChapterIds` was a plain `Set`, while `prefetchingChapterIds` and `failedChapterIds` were `$state(Set)`. Harmless today but inconsistent.
2. Two `queueMicrotask` calls were waiting for Svelte's reactive flush — `await tick()` is the correct primitive, since the reactive update may settle later than a single microtask hop.
3. Six places mutated `Set` state via `new Set(old).add(x)` / `delete(x)` boilerplate.
4. The keymap was a 10-condition `if/else if` chain in `onKey`. Not testable, not extensible.
5. `pageGroups`, `currentChapterFirstIndex`, `chapterPageCount`, `nextChapterIdAfter`, and `prevChapterIdBefore` were all inline in the `.svelte` file — pure logic with no unit-test coverage. That's exactly where the Kaiju "11 / 19" indicator bug and the cascading-prefetch bug lived.
6. Three derived chains (`currentChapterFirstIndex` → `chapterPageCount` → `pageInChapter`) each rescanned `loadedPages`. Consolidated into one.

### What changed

**New module `lib/readerLogic.ts`** holds the pure logic, with **`lib/readerLogic.test.ts`** covering it:

- `buildPageGroups(pages, mode)` — single / double / double-cover grouping
- `scanChapterBounds(pages, currentIndex)` — chapter-local first index + count
- `chapterIdAfter(chapters, id)` / `chapterIdBefore(chapters, id)` — preserves publication order, doesn't sort by id
- `findGroupContainingPage(groups, pageIndex)` — used by resume + pageMode toggle
- `keyToReaderAction(key)` — keymap, returns a tagged union

The reader page now imports and composes these. Inline implementations are gone.

**`loadedChapterIds`** is now `$state(new Set())`. Updates via `setWith` / `setWithout` helpers that the prefetching/failed sets also use.

**`queueMicrotask` → `await tick()`** in the resume-position scroll and the pageMode toggle.

**`onKey`** is now seven lines: lookup the action via `keyToReaderAction`, switch on it.

**19 new vitest cases** for the extracted helpers:

- `buildPageGroups`: empty input, single mode, double mode (even / odd counts), pairs-don't-cross-chapter-boundaries, double-cover mode, cover-offset-resets-per-chapter
- `scanChapterBounds`: bounds for each chapter, ex → #077 regression for the Kaiju bug, out-of-range fallback
- `chapterIdAfter` / `chapterIdBefore`: publication order preserved with non-monotonic IDs, end / unknown / empty cases
- `findGroupContainingPage`: range coverage, out-of-range
- `keyToReaderAction`: every binding (scroll, flip, toggles, escape), case sensitivity, null for unmapped keys

41 tests total now pass (22 existing + 19 new). Build clean, clippy clean.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.4
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.4

Hardened chapter loading. Stops the prefetch cascade and gives every failure a recovery path.

### What was broken

Several things at once when a prefetch hit a slow or failing API:

1. **Cascade**: `Promise.race` between the invoke and a 12 s timeout returned control as soon as the timeout fired, but the underlying invoke was still in flight. `fetchingNext` got reset, and the next `$effect` tick re-called `maybePrefetchNext` — which started **another** invoke for the same chapter. Both eventually completed. With multiple page moves the same thing happened for the chapter after that, and so on.
2. **No cooldown on failure**: a chapter that timed out got retried on every page move forever.
3. **No timeout on initial load**: a hung first fetch sat on the spinner indefinitely.
4. **$effect spam**: a single reactive effect handled chapter-read tracking, page-position saving, AND prefetch — so every reactive dep change (including a successful prefetch's append) immediately re-fired the prefetch check.
5. **No retry path**: failed prefetch was logged to console.warn and forgotten. The user just saw a spinner stop or never start.

### What changed

Three sets now coordinate chapter loading:

- `loadedChapterIds` — chapters whose pages are already in `loadedPages`
- `prefetchingChapterIds` — chapter IDs currently being fetched
- `failedChapterIds` — chapter IDs whose last fetch failed

A new `fetchChapter()` helper wraps `invoke('get_chapter_pages')` with the 12 s timeout and returns `null` on timeout/error rather than throwing. Both `loadInitial` and `maybePrefetchNext` go through it. `fetchingNext` is now a `$derived` of `prefetchingChapterIds.size > 0`, so multiple chapters in flight register correctly and a stale flag is impossible.

`maybePrefetchNext` checks all three sets before kicking off:
- already loaded? skip
- already in flight? skip
- failed previously (and not a forced retry)? skip

`$effect` is split. Prefetch is now in its own tiny effect that depends only on `currentPage` — page moves are the only trigger, and the same `currentPage` never fires twice.

`loadInitial` gets the same 12 s timeout and now surfaces a clear error with a **↻ Retry** button instead of an infinite spinner.

At end-of-loaded-scroll: if the next chapter is known but failed, the footer shows a labelled retry block:

> Couldn't load **#089**.
> May be rate-limited or temporarily unavailable.
> ↻ Retry #089

Clicking retry clears the failure flag and re-fetches with `force: true`.

The background prefetch indicator now names the chapter being pulled: "loading next chapter (#089)…" — so it's clear what's happening without scrolling.

### Net effect

- One inflight fetch per chapter, ever.
- Failed chapter doesn't re-fire on its own — needs a deliberate retry click.
- Initial load can't hang forever.
- The runaway "stack of chapter dividers" state from v0.7.3 isn't reachable.

body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.3

Real fix for the page indicator on chapter transitions.

### What v0.7.2 still got wrong

v0.7.2 computed the current chapter's first index by `findIndex` over `loadedPages` with `p.chapterId === visibleChapterId`. The intent was right: scope the indicator to the chapter the user is reading. But `visibleChapterId` and `loadedPages` are both derived from reactive state, and during Svelte's update pass they can momentarily disagree. When that happened, `findIndex` returned -1, `Math.max(0, -1)` silently masked it as 0, and the indicator reported `currentPageIndex + 1` instead of the chapter-local page number.

Confirmed by probing Kaiju No. 8 around the **ex → #077** boundary:

```
[91] id=1015153 name="ex"    ← in loadedPages at indices 0..9
[92] id=1015155 name="#077"  ← in loadedPages at indices 10..28
```

Crossing into #077 should show "1 / 19". v0.7.2 showed "11 / 19" — exactly `currentPageIndex (=10) + 1`. The header chapter name correctly switched to "#077", because that derivation reads from `loadedPages[currentPageIndex].chapterName` and doesn't take the findIndex code path.

### What changed

Chapter bounds are now computed by scanning backward/forward from `currentPageIndex` directly, since chapter pages are always contiguous (we `appendChapter()` whole chapters at a time and never insert anywhere but the end):

- `currentChapterFirstIndex` walks left while the previous page shares the same `chapterId`.
- `chapterPageCount` walks right while the next page shares the same `chapterId`.

body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.2

Page indicator + progress bar are now per-chapter, not session-global.

### What was broken

The header indicator and footer progress bar both displayed `currentPage / loadedPages.length`. `currentPage` was a running count across *all* loaded chapters, and `loadedPages.length` was the sum of every chapter that had been auto-prefetched in the session.

So if chapter A had 108 pages and you crossed into chapter B (43 pages, just auto-loaded), landing on page 1 of B showed up as **"109 / 151"**. The progress bar filled to ~72%. The user just started a chapter — the UI said they were three-quarters of the way through it.

### What changed

Added derived state for the chapter the user is *actually* reading:

- `currentChapterFirstIndex` — index in `loadedPages` of the current chapter's first page
- `chapterPageCount` — count of pages in the current chapter only
- `pageInChapter` — 1-indexed page within the current chapter

The header indicator now shows `pageInChapter / chapterPageCount` (and `pageInChapter-(pageInChapter+1) / chapterPageCount` in double-page mode). The progress bar fills based on the same ratio. Crossing a chapter boundary resets the counter to 1/N and the bar to its starting position.

Per-chapter resume continues to work — that code was already converting to chapter-local before saving, but it now uses the same `pageInChapter` derived state for consistency.

## FRANK MANGA+ v0.7.0

Eye-protection sepia filter for night reading.

### What's new

Reading manga on a bright LCD at night gets harsh — pure-white speech-bubble backgrounds in particular. The reader header now has a **crescent-moon toggle** (next to the page-layout icon) that cycles through four warmth levels:

| Level | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| off | unchanged, default |
| low | subtle amber tint, like a slight warm-toned monitor |
| med | noticeable sepia, like a hardware "night light" mode |
| high | heavy amber-sepia, late-night reading |

Press **`F`** to cycle through, or click the moon icon. The button shows one to three dots indicating the level. Persisted in localStorage so the choice survives reloads and chapter switches.

### How the filter works

CSS `filter: sepia(N) brightness(M) saturate(P)` applied to the whole page-stack. Sepia shifts hue toward amber without flattening the luminance range, so blacks stay black, whites become a warm cream/sepia, and the contrast of the artwork is preserved. Brightness and saturation dial in extra warmth at the higher levels.

Color manga (JoJo, etc.) keeps a recognizable palette at the low level and progressively desaturates toward the high level — that's intentional for night reading.

name: FRANK MANGA+ v0.6.9
body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.6.9

Two reader navigation fixes.

### Space bar at the chapter boundary now actually crosses into the new chapter

`advance('forward', 'scroll')` at the end of the loaded scroll called `maybePrefetchNext(true)` to pull the next chapter, then `goToGroupIndex(currentGroup + 1)` to scroll into its first group. The await on the prefetch returned synchronously as soon as the pages were appended, but Svelte's `bind:this={frameEls[gi]}` hadn't run yet — so `frameEls[currentGroup + 1]` was still undefined, and `scrollIntoView` silently no-op'd on a missing element.

Mouse-wheel scrolling worked because the wheel just moves `scrollTop` and doesn't touch `frameEls`. Space, ArrowDown, j, PageDown all sat at the same page while the next chapter was loaded but invisible.

Fix: `await tick()` after the prefetch and before the scroll, so Svelte flushes the new bindings first.

### Click zones use left-based positioning + explicit z-index

Past reports had clicks anywhere on the page seeming to only advance forward, with the "back" zone (right half) not responding. The likely cause was the right zone's `right: 0; width: 50%` getting reinterpreted by the page-frame's flex layout in double-pair mode — the absolute-positioned button can interact oddly with flex contexts on some renderers.

The fix makes both zones left-based (`left: 0` and `left: 50%`), adds an explicit `z-index: 2` so they always sit above the manga page and any flex siblings, and stops click propagation defensively. Should be solid across single and double-pair modes.

## FRANK MANGA+ v0.6.8

Follow-up to v0.6.7's chapter-list fix.

### What was still broken

v0.6.7 swapped `viewer.chapters` (3 entries, truncated) for `title_detail.chapter_list_v2` (canonical full list, 150 entries for Kaiju No. 8) — but it still sorted that list by `chapterId` ascending. Live probe against Kaiju surfaced a problem with that sort:

```
sorted by chapter_id, around the boundary:
  id=1023544 name="#123"
  id=1023808 name="#125"    ← lower id, higher chapter number
  id=1024011 name="#124"    ← higher id, lower chapter number
  id=1024314 name="#126"
```

Chapter 125 has a *lower* `chapterId` than chapter 124. Probably because the API reassigned ids during a re-upload at some point. The reading order is 123 → 124 → 125 → 126, but the id ordering says 123 → 125 → 124 → 126.

So v0.6.7 would have unblocked your specific chapter 54 → 55 navigation (whose ids *are* monotonic), but for Kaiju readers around chapter 124–125 the auto-advance would still send you into the wrong chapter.

### What changed

The canonical `chapter_list_v2` arrives in publication order already (that's how `title_detail` returns it). v0.6.8 drops the sort and preserves the natural order. Auto-advance now visits chapters in the order Shueisha published them, regardless of internal id reshuffles.

The viewer.chapters fallback (still used for the first ~1 s before `title_detail` arrives) is still sorted by id — it's only ever the first three chapters of the title, where ids and numbers are monotonic.

## FRANK MANGA+ v0.6.7

Fix for the bogus end-of-title indicator on mid-title chapters.

### What was broken

The reader's auto-advance and the manual "Load next chapter" + "end-of-title" indicators all read from `MangaViewer.chapters` — the chapter list field on the `manga_viewer_v3` API response. That field looked like the full title's chapter list at a glance, but isn't.

Confirmed with a live probe against Kaiju No. 8 chapter 54:

```
=== title_detail ===
chapter_list_v2: 150 entries
first 3 chapter ids: [(1007603, "#001"), (1007604, "#002"), (1007605, "#003")]
last 3 chapter ids:  [(1025957, "#129"), (1024792, "#128"), (1024791, "#127")]

=== manga_viewer_v3 for chapter 54 (id=1012576) ===
viewer.chapters: 3 entries
viewer chapter ids: [1007603, 1007604, 1007605]
```

`title_detail` returns the full 150-chapter sequence. `manga_viewer_v3` returns only the first 3, regardless of which chapter you're reading. So `nextChapterIdAfter(1012576)` searched `[1007603, 1007604, 1007605]`, didn't find the current chapter, returned null — and the reader showed "You've reached the end" on chapter 54 of a series that has 129 chapters.

### What changed

When the reader mounts, it kicks off `get_title_detail` for the title in parallel with the page load. As soon as that response arrives (typically ~1 s after pages start streaming), the chapter list is swapped from the truncated `viewer.chapters` to the canonical full list from `chapterListV2` (falling back to `chapterListGroup` for the segmented case).

Auto-advance and the end-of-title indicator now both consult the canonical list. Chapter 54 → chapter 55 works. Same fix applies to every series where the user is past chapter 3 — Kaiju No. 8 was just the most visible symptom.

The viewer chapter list is still used in the first second before `title_detail` returns, so initial nav within the first few chapters works immediately without waiting.

### Other

- Also threads the `lang` URL param into the reader so the new `get_title_detail` call uses the same language tuple as the title page that linked here.

body:
## FRANK MANGA+ v0.6.6

Two reader QoL touches.

### Resume reading position per chapter

If you leave a chapter mid-read and come back to it later — either via the "Continue ▶" button on the title page, the chapter list, or any other path that loads `/reader/<chapterId>` — the reader now scrolls you back to the page you were on instead of starting from page 1.

Tracked per-chapter in localStorage. The page-position update fires whenever the visible page changes, so it's always up to date by the time you navigate away. Restoration happens immediately after the chapter's pages load, with an instant scroll so you don't see a visible animation from page 1.

If you've never visited a chapter before, or saved position is page 1, it behaves exactly like before.

### End-of-title is now obviously the end

When you reach the last chapter and try to scroll further, you used to see a small muted line of text: `— end of available chapters —`. Easy to mistake for a loading stall.

Now it's a centered card with:

> 🏁
>
> **You've reached the end**
>
> No further chapters are available right now. New releases drop on the schedule MANGA Plus publishes — check back later.
>
> `[ Back to title page ]`

Clear that the reader didn't stall, plus a one-click way back to the title page to pick something else.
